sections.h2: Which parts of a Columbus sale slow things down?
sections.html:
Delays usually trace back to steps that rest on someone else: a lender's approval, an appraiser's schedule, or a repair list that grows after the inspection. A direct cash sale sidesteps most of these, while a well-priced listing can still move briskly in Franklin County.

Whichever route you take, settle three facts early: the payoff on any mortgage, the year's tax status, and the school district and municipality for the parcel. Columbus sprawls over so many districts and suburban borders that buyers raise all three almost at once.

sections.h2: Why is Columbus so large, and why does the boundary matter?
sections.html:
Columbus has the largest land area of any city in Ohio, a result of annexing suburbs that needed city water lines. In total the city measures about 223 square miles; QuickFacts counts 220.04 of them as land, with 4,116 people per square mile at the 2020 census.

The city was founded on February 14, 1812 as a planned capital near the center of the state, at the forks of the Scioto River, and became a borough on February 10, 1816. The National Road reached it from Baltimore in 1831, and the Ohio and Erie Canal link helped growth along with it. Growth has continued: 938,396 residents by the Census Bureau's mid-2025 estimate, a 3.6% gain on the 906,215 base of April 2020 and far above the 787,033 counted in 2010.

Annexation crossed many school and township lines, so a Columbus address may fall in Columbus City Schools or in South-Western, Dublin, Hilliard, New Albany-Plain, Westerville or Worthington. Print the right district on your listing sheet. Columbus City Schools alone runs 142 elementary, middle and high schools, among them several magnet schools, and the suburban districts typically serve one or more townships, sometimes crossing municipal lines. A buyer with children will check the boundary against the district's own map, so give the street address exactly as the county records it.

sections.h2: Which Columbus neighborhoods do buyers ask about most?
sections.html:
Columbus is sometimes called a city of neighborhoods. The Arena District, Brewery District, Clintonville, Franklinton, German Village, the Short North and Victorian Village are the best-known, and each carries its own housing stock and buyer base. Victorian Village is known for Victorian houses facing Goodale Park. In the 1800s a wave of German immigrants settled on cheap land south of downtown, and Irish residents settled to the north.

  • Core neighborhoods: confirm the exact name buyers use for your block, since listings are searched by neighborhood.
  • Outer areas: confirm the school district and whether the parcel is inside Columbus or a neighboring suburb.
  • Riverside and creek-side parcels: the region has a history of flooding, including the Great Flood of 1913, so ask the city or county about flood-zone status before you list a low-lying house.

sections.h2: What do Columbus home values and household figures look like?
sections.html:
The median owner-occupied home in Columbus is valued at $252,900 on the 2020-2024 survey, above the figures for Cincinnati and Cleveland. Owners occupy 44.1% of homes across 390,528 households that average 2.28 people. Typical monthly rent is $1,295, the middle household earns $66,082, and 38.2% of adults 25 and older hold at least a bachelor's degree.

Retail sales came to $32,813 per resident in 2022, well above Cincinnati, Cleveland or Cleveland Heights. Government is the largest single source of local jobs, since Columbus is the state capital, and Ohio State University and its Wexner Medical Center, Nationwide Children's Hospital, Nationwide Mutual Insurance, American Electric Power and Battelle are among the other big employers.

sections.h2: What will the Franklin County Auditor collect when the deed transfers?
sections.html:
The Auditor's calculator page prints a conveyance fee of $3 per $1,000, split between $1 from the state and $2 from the county commissioners. The table repeats each item as printed there.

Franklin County Auditor transfer tax and conveyance fee schedule
ChargeAs printed by the Auditor
Conveyance fee$3 per $1,000 of the sale price
Conveyance fee when the grantor receives the homestead exemption$1 per $1,000, because the county's permissive part is waived
Minimum conveyance fee$3
Transfer tax$0.50 on every non-exempt transfer
Exempt transfersOnly the $0.50 transfer tax
Accepted paymentCash, business check or cashier's check payable to the Franklin County Auditor

The office turns away personal checks, and its calculator wants the sale amount rounded up to the next $100. The department moves more than 30,000 transfers each year; its number is 614-525-3253. Exempt categories come from Ohio Revised Code 319.202 and 319.54(G)(3).

sections.h2: How do Columbus streets and highways shape the way buyers see a house?
sections.html:
The street grid starts at Broad and High Streets downtown, with house numbers rising outward and about 700 numbers to the mile. Interstate 70 runs east and west, Interstate 71 runs north and southwest, and the two share about a mile and a half downtown at the spot locals call The Split, a known rush-hour choke point. Workers average 21.5 minutes to get to a job, the shortest commute of the four cities in QuickFacts' comparison.

Tell buyers how far the house is from the nearest interstate ramp and whether it sits near the Split, since both change the commute they imagine.

sections.h2: How do the tax bill and homestead exemption fit into a Franklin County closing?
sections.html:
For 2026, the treasurer's site named July 20 as the last day before penalty and interest, and said a missing bill does not excuse a late payment. Owners with no bill in hand are told to call 614-525-3438. On your side of the table, the closing statement divides the tax between buyer and seller, and your escrow officer can walk through that entry.

The standard homestead exemption is a credit aimed at older or disabled owners: age 65 by the end of the year being applied for, or total and permanent disability on January 1, plus primary residence and a qualifying income. A richer version with no income test goes to veterans rated 100% disabled from service, and it removes the tax on $50,000 of appraised value. Because a seller who holds the exemption cuts the conveyance fee to $1 per $1,000, check the Auditor's property search for the Homestead Credit status before closing.

  • Auditor's property search: shows whether the Homestead Credit applies to your parcel.
  • Treasurer: confirms the status of the year's tax and any bill you did not receive.
  • Closing statement: shows the buyer-seller tax split before you sign.

sections.h2: How do short-term rental permits and the disclosure form apply here?
sections.html:
Nightly rentals in Columbus run through the License Section of Building and Zoning Services, 4252 Groves Road, phone 614-645-8366, which issues the short-term rental permit. A house that was ever advertised on a booking platform invites buyer questions about that permit.

Revised Code 5302.30 sets the disclosure form for residences of up to four units, excusing court-ordered sales, estate fiduciaries and gifts to direct-line relatives. Climate matters here too: Columbus is humid continental and sits in USDA hardiness zone 6b, with relatively light winter snow because it lies too far south and west for much lake-effect snow, and severe thunderstorms and the occasional tornado can hit in spring, so known roof or hail damage belongs on the disclosure form.

faqs.q: How are conveyance fees figured in Franklin County?
faqs.a: At $3 for each $1,000 of price, with a $3 floor and a $0.50 transfer tax. A grantor who holds the homestead exemption at transfer pays $1 per $1,000 instead.

faqs.q: Does the Auditor take personal checks?
faqs.a: No. Cash, business checks and cashier's checks made out to the Franklin County Auditor are accepted, and the amount must be exact or the transfer will not process.

faqs.q: Could my Columbus house be in a suburban school district?
faqs.a: Yes, depending on the parcel. Columbus City Schools is the biggest system at 55,000 pupils, yet parts of the city belong to South-Western, Dublin, Hilliard, New Albany-Plain, Westerville or Worthington. Check your tax bill or ask the county.

faqs.q: My Columbus house used to be a short-term rental. Does that affect the sale?
faqs.a: The permit applies to operating the rental, and the License Section of Building and Zoning Services issues it. Ask that office at 614-645-8366 whether yours is current, since a buyer is likely to ask.

faqs.q: What if my Franklin County tax bill never arrived?
faqs.a: Call the treasurer at 614-525-3438. The office's site warns that a bill that never showed up does not erase penalty and interest.
